summary: This article explains how mosaic art is made from small pieces of tile, glass, or stone arranged into pictures and patterns, examples from ancient and modern times, and the patience and planning the work takes.
introduce: Show the title “Mosaic Art: Pictures from Pieces” and give pairs one minute to list everything they already know about this topic. Share a few ideas on the board, then tell students to check which ideas the article confirms.

keyTerms.def: one small piece of stone, glass, or tile used to make a mosaic
a plan that shows how something will look when it is finished
from a time very long ago

challengeTerms.def: having many small, detailed parts arranged in a complex way
the way the parts of a piece of art are arranged together
the careful work of repairing something old so it looks whole again

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that making art from many small pieces takes more patience than painting a picture all at once? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a craftsman plans and builds a mosaic.
struggling: Pre-teach tessera, design, and ancient with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses intricate, composition, and restoration to connect the article to something they learned in another subject.
